title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 111
paragraphs: When his turn at last came round, the Athenians were drawn up for battle in the following order. On the right wing was the polemarch Callimachus (the Athenian custom then being that the polemarch commanded the right wing); next after him, in order, came the tribes arranged by their numbers, one after the other; and last, drawn up on the left wing, were the Plataeans. Ever since this battle, when the Athenians offer sacrifices at the solemn assemblies of the four-yearly festivals, the Athenian herald prays “that blessings may come to the Athenians and to the Plataeans alike.” On this occasion, as the Athenians were forming up at Marathon, something like this was done: their line, made equal in length to the Median line, came to be of only a few ranks' depth in the middle — the weakest point — while each wing was given greater numbers and so reinforced.
